title: What Startups Are Really Like: 19 founder surprises that all trace back to "a startup is not a job"
summary: Paul Graham surveyed 100+ YC founders on what surprised them about starting a startup, which amounts to asking what he got wrong. The surprises (cofounder character, persistence, slow deals, minimal launches, talking to users, luck, clueless investors) were all things he already says, because people unconsciously model a startup on a job.

principles.text: Pick cofounders for character and commitment, not ability, then work hard to maintain the relationship.
principles.quote: What people wished they'd paid more attention to when choosing cofounders was character and commitment, not ability. This was particularly true with startups that failed. The lesson: don't pick cofounders who will flake.

principles.text: Persistence matters more than raw intelligence, and everything takes longer than you expect.
principles.quote: Several founders mentioned specifically how much more important persistence was than intelligence.

principles.text: Launch the simplest possible version. If trolls don't make fun of your first version, you waited too long.
principles.quote: If your first version is so impressive that trolls don't make fun of it, you waited too long to launch.

principles.text: Treat the initial version as a trick to get users talking to you; product development is a conversation with users.
principles.quote: Product development is a conversation with the user that doesn't really start till you launch.

principles.text: Treat your idea as a hypothesis, not a blueprint. Determination without flexibility can trap you in a local maximum.
principles.quote: We've always encouraged founders to see a startup idea as a hypothesis rather than a blueprint.

principles.text: Assume deals fall through and you won't get investor money; be optimistic only about what you control.
principles.quote: The mistake is to be optimistic about things you can't control. By all means be optimistic about your ability to make something great.
